subject: economics
title: Cartels and Competition Policy
welcome_lead: Cartels cheat consumers - regulators fight back.
meta_desc: A-Level Oligopoly: cartels and competition policy.
final_note: Most cartels eventually collapse - but only after damage to consumers.

concepts.def: Group of firms colluding to raise prices.
Each member can profit by undercutting privately.
Regulator offers reduced fines to whistle-blowers.
Body enforcing competition law - UK CMA, EU Commission.
Share of market held by top N firms (e.g. CR4).
Reviewing proposed mergers for competitive harm.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each cartel member has private incentive to cheat by undercutting the cartel price. Detection requires effort; lenient treatment for whistle-blowers makes the cartel unstable.
The UK CMA and EU Commission investigate cartels and mergers. Fines can reach 10 percent of global turnover; criminal sanctions exist for individuals.
Authorities use concentration ratios and the Herfindahl Index to assess market power. Large mergers that would create dominance can be blocked or required to divest.

options: Reward the first cartel member to confess
